title: Fractal quantum many-body scars and Hamiltonian inverse design from ZX-calculus
abstract: Diagrammatic languages such as ZX-calculus provide compact and intuitive descriptions of quantum processes and have become established tools for circuit simplification, verification, and compilation. However, their potential as a framework for constructing many-body states and the Hamiltonians that host them remains largely unexplored. Here, we introduce families of fractal many-body states obtained from ZX-diagrams based on the Sierpiński triangle and Sierpiński carpet. By construction, the underlying graph connectivity imposes atypical subvolume-law minimum-cut upper bounds on the entanglement, while the actual states are parametrically less entangled still: the triangle family obeys an area law, whereas the carpet family displays approximately logarithmic scaling across the available system sizes. Additionally, their local observables retain fractal-like spatial structure, identifying these states as natural candidates for atypical eigenstates in otherwise thermalizing systems. For the triangle family, we combine parent-Hamiltonian methods, insights from ZX-calculus, and local ZX identities that certify exact annihilation of the target state, producing frustration-free Hamiltonians whose terms admit simple representations in the same diagrammatic language as the states themselves. We then construct a local deformation that produces chaotic level statistics while embedding the fractal ZX state in the bulk of the energy spectrum as an exact quantum many-body scar. Our results demonstrate, through this explicit construction, that ZX-calculus can serve as a framework for Hamiltonian inverse design, in which quantum many-body scars, their local annihilators, and the chaotic Hamiltonians embedding them can be constructed and related through a set of graphical identities.
summary: This paper introduces a powerful framework using ZX-calculus to design quantum many-body scars based on fractal geometries. By constructing these states and their associated Hamiltonians analytically, the authors demonstrate how to embed exact, atypical eigenstates into otherwise chaotic energy spectra. This provides a novel, diagrammatically verifiable route for Hamiltonian inverse design in condensed matter physics.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a systematic framework using ZX-calculus for Hamiltonian inverse design, specifically constructing quantum many-body scars (QMBS) that are atypical eigenstates embedded within otherwise thermalizing systems.
main_result: The paper demonstrates that the ZX-calculus can serve as this inverse design tool, allowing the explicit construction and mathematical relationship between fractal scar states, their local annihilators, and the chaotic Hamiltonians embedding them.
method: The authors utilize diagrammatic languages (ZX-calculus) to encode fractal many-body states derived from Sierpiński structures. They combine these with parent-Hamiltonian techniques and local ZX identities to construct exact scars and then deform the Hamiltonian to induce chaos while preserving the scar state.
model_or_system: The model involves quantum many-body systems whose states are represented by fractal patterns (Sierpiński triangle/carpet) encoded in ZX-diagrams. The dynamics are governed by Hamiltonians constructed via local terms derived from these diagrams, allowing for embedding into chaotic spectra.
key_observables: Entanglement entropy (showing area law or logarithmic scaling), local expectation values ($\langle X_i angle$), and spectral statistics (diagnosing transition between Poissonian/integrable and Wigner-Dyson/chaotic regimes).
important_parameters: The fractal generation parameter ($g$) defining the level of self-similarity, and system size ($L$).
main_assumptions: It is assumed that the ZX-calculus provides a sufficiently rigorous graphical language to certify both the state structure and the Hamiltonian constraints (annihilation conditions).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the methodology: selecting fractal ZX-diagrams as scars, using parent Hamiltonians/local identities for construction, and showing entanglement entropy scaling ($	ext{S}$ vs. bipartition ratio) for triangle (area law) and carpet (logarithmic scaling) families.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the use of ZX-calculus for state representation; then, it details the fractal construction of states with specific entanglement properties; subsequently, it applies parent-Hamiltonian methods to find annihilators; finally, it constructs a local deformation to embed these scars into chaotic Hamiltonians.
why_interesting: This work bridges advanced diagrammatic quantum computation tools (ZX-calculus) directly into condensed matter theory by providing an explicit, constructive method for generating non-trivial, non-thermal eigenstates (scars) in complex many-body systems.
